q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of a cushion cover?
title: Cushion cover carbon footprint per piece
short: Take the fabric per cover, including cutting waste, and multiply by your mill's per-metre or per-kg figure. Add zips, piping, any embroidery or print, stitching, pressing and packing, then divide the unit's energy by covers passed.
audience: Home textile makers and exporters, including Karur and Panipat units

ul: Face and back fabric per cover from the cutting plan.
Embroidery thread or print paste, where used.

p: Report per cover by size, and keep the filler cushion separate if you sell it filled.

example.title: Worked example: home textile unit per cover (one month)
lines: Plant total: 10,650 / 60,000 = 0.177 kg CO2 per cover
Add fabric and trims for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
